newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen range trading.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen range trading.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower in thin Tuesday trade as players cashed in some of their gains in the absence of fresh leads ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan business sentiment survey.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended 160 points lower at 20,650 after hitting an early high of 20,820 on volume of 8,290 lots.
A trader with a Japanese futures house said the contract was likely to trade a 20,500-21,000 range if there were no fresh developments until the tankan release on June 25.
Dealers said the yen's relatively stronger stance on Tuesday had a limited impact on the market.

Another dealer said players liquidated long positions following a lack of buying interest despite a net three million shares of buy orders from foreign investors through Japan's Big Four securities houses in the underlying cash market.
"We didn't see people putting a lot of buying orders in the futures market despite the orders in the cash market," he said.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 368.0 against its opening 367.8 on volume of 881 lots.
